$comment: Invariant ids owned by the P2 task `p2-validate-sample-ci`. The list is EMPTY, and that is the correct state. This lane owns the validator SUITE (the runner, the report, V10-V12), the stratified reviewer sample, `coursekit sign`, and the `build-es` / `validate-es` jobs in pack-ci.yml. Two independent reasons nothing is claimed here. First, `scripts/coverage-map.ts` scans `packages`, `apps` and `e2e` for owning tests; `tools/` is deliberately outside that walk, so a Python test cannot be an owning test and claiming an id here would mean claiming one with no owner. Second, the ids this work will eventually back are properties of a produced pack — INV-PACK-15 wants codec, bitrate and bytes on a real bank; INV-PACK-17 wants an attribution string reachable from a rendered credits surface; INV-PACK-18 wants a device refusing an unverified pack; INV-PACK-54 wants a subsetted font file in apps/mobile — and none of those exist until G0-G9 and the app-side installer land. Claiming one now would mean writing a test that asserts a dict has a key and naming it INV-PACK-18, which is the 'owning test that proves nothing' the plan's rule 4 is written against.

crossLaneContracts.consumedBy: .github/workflows/pack-ci.yml, the `Collect the pack artefacts` step of `validate-es`
crossLaneContracts.assertion: the file exists under that exact name; the step prints `::error::...is missing` and exits 1 otherwise
crossLaneContracts.why: nothing in tools/coursekit defines this filename. config/package.py is empty by design and owned by the G9 lane, so `es.pack` is a string this lane WROTE DOWN rather than imported. If G9 names its SQLite output anything else — `pack.sqlite`, `es-0.1.0.pack` — `validate-es` fails at the collect step and the failure reads as a missing build rather than as a disagreement about a name. Move it into a shared constant the moment G9 defines one.

crossLaneContracts.consumedBy: the same collect step, and `coursekit sign <lang>`
crossLaneContracts.assertion: MANIFEST_FILENAME == 'manifest.json' and PACK_STAGE_ID == 'g9' both already exist in coursekit.config, so this half of the path IS imported, not written down
crossLaneContracts.why: the manifest is what `sign` signs and what S137's provenance block renders

crossLaneContracts.assertion: an ABSENT rtl meta row is a blocking finding, not a false: nobody having decided is not the same as having decided LTR
crossLaneContracts.why: RTL_LANGUAGES is empty today, so for es the correct value is false — but V12 must fail a pack that never wrote the row at all, or the first language that needs true ships without it

crossLaneContracts.producedBy: G4, G0, G5, G7, G2 respectively
crossLaneContracts.consumedBy: shipped_items() — the join V10/V11/V12 and `coursekit sample` all read
crossLaneContracts.assertion: a missing artefact raises SuiteInputMissing and becomes a blocking finding; it is never an empty pass
crossLaneContracts.why: these are the inter-stage contract frozen by p2/deps-scaffold; this lane reads them and writes none of them

heldWithoutAnInvariantId: The suite cannot report a pass it did not earn, and all three ways it could are refused by name in validators/runner.py with a falsifier each in tests/test_validate_runner.py: an UNREGISTERED validator is exit 2 and an `unregistered` row in the report (the denominator is config.VALIDATOR_IDS, never the registry — a report that omitted the unwritten validator would print '16/16 green' on the S002 card); a SKIPPED validator whose dependency group is absent is exit 3 and blocking; a validator that RAISES is exit 4. test_green_is_not_vacuous proves the success path is still reachable, because a runner that failed unconditionally would pass every refusal test in the file

V10, V11 and V12 each FAIL on an empty or absent input rather than passing fast. The shared join `shipped_items()` raises when `selected_item` or `ingested_sentence` is missing, and each validator turns that into a blocking finding. tests/test_validators_pack.py::test_v10_fails_on_an_empty_pack_rather_than_passing_fast is the falsifier: zero sentences produce zero findings, and zero findings is exactly what a green validator returns — the same shape docs/ci.md describes for `maestro test` over an empty directory

V10 separates three failures that have three different fixes: an unresolved licence (NOASSERTION / UNKNOWN / empty), a licence that resolved to a real string off the allow-list (CC BY-NC-ND, the licence that cut TED2020 — a check that only looked for empty fields would pass it), and a resolved licence whose attribution owner is missing, which is INV-PACK-17 failing at the credits surface instead of here

V11's difficulty is a DECLARED PROXY with named weights in config/validate.py, recomputed by hand in a test, and its banded-token coverage is measured and reported. Below MIN_BANDED_TOKEN_COVERAGE the validator emits a warning saying the number is a length signal rather than a vocabulary one, because the banded table is keyed by lemma and the proxy reads surface tokens — a validator that quietly reported the weaker number as the stronger one would be the drift it is looking for

V12 is the PACK half of INV-PACK-54 and says so: it proves no pack string carries a character outside the shipped font's declared ranges (for Spanish that is á é í ó ú ñ ü ¿ ¡ and their upper case, asserted against the ranges themselves so a future narrowing fails there rather than at the first ¿ a learner sees), and it records `bundled_font_subset_checked: false` in its runlog entry. The other half — that the .ttf actually shipped in apps/mobile still carries those ranges after subsetting — is P3's, because the subset lives with the app

V12 fails an ABSENT direction flag as well as a wrong one. `rtl` missing from the pack's meta rows is not `false`, it is nobody having decided, and the first pack that needs `true` would ship without it

The reviewer sample is stratified over (unit_index, exercise_type, provenance) and deterministic under a recorded seed. A measured bug is pinned by test_a_budget_smaller_than_the_strata_still_reaches_the_last_unit: 5 units x 8 exercise types x 2 provenances is ~80 strata, and a 40-row sheet allocated one-each in lexicographic key order filled up inside units 1-4 and drew nothing from unit 5 — the unit built on the most accumulated vocabulary, which is where drift lands. Allocation now round-robins over units, numerically so `10` does not sort before `2`

The wrong-item rate never leaves the tool without its provenance. PROVISIONAL_DEFECT_RATE_NOTE is one constant because the string has to be identical on the S001 card, in the manifest, in docs/pack-provenance.md and in tools/coursekit/README.md; summarise() cannot emit a rate without it, only reviewer_kind == 'paid-native-speaker' clears it, an unscored sample has a rate of None (which does not pass the 2% gate — None is not 0%), and `awkward` verdicts are published separately rather than folded into the number the gate is about

`coursekit sign` verifies what it just wrote against the COMMITTED public key, and verify_manifest refuses a manifest signed by any other key. A manifest that carries its own public key and verifies against it proves that somebody owned *a* key, which is what an attacker who re-signed a modified pack also has; test_a_manifest_signed_by_another_key_is_refused shows the self-consistent check passing and the trusted check failing on the same bytes. The private key is only ever the PACK_SIGNING_KEY CI secret: a PEM block or a path in that variable is refused by name, and `coursekit sign --help` carries no --key flag

The Python and TypeScript halves of the signing contract are pinned to each other: tests/test_signing.py reads packages/schema/src/signing.ts and asserts the key path, the secret name, the algorithm, the 44-byte SPKI length and the 12-byte ed25519 OID prefix all match, so a rename on either side fails the build instead of producing packs no device can verify

A registry bug that would have poisoned every later P2 lane, found and fixed here: `Registry.reset_for_tests()` cleared `_discovered` but registration is a side effect of IMPORTING a module, and importlib returns a cached module without re-running it — so the next discover() was a no-op and every test after the first user of the `empty_registry` fixture saw a permanently empty registry whatever the package contained. Measured before the fix: register V10-V12, reset, ask again, get (). reset_for_tests now suppresses discovery so 'empty' stays empty, and a new restore_for_tests() evicts the discovered modules from sys.modules so registrations re-run

.github/workflows/pack-ci.yml gains `build-es` and `validate-es`, guarded by a `pipeline-ready` job in the shape of native-e2e's `flows-present`: the G-stages and validators are counted on a ten-second runner first, the two long jobs are skipped rather than run over an empty registry, and the artefact upload uses `if-no-files-found: error` so `es-pack-<sha>` can never be an empty archive that reads as a successful build

knownHazards.what: `Registry.restore_for_tests()` (coursekit/__init__.py) evicts the discovered stage/validator modules from sys.modules so their registrations re-run on the next import. The re-import defines a SECOND `SuiteInputMissing` class object, while `coursekit/sample.py` bound the name at its own import time.
knownHazards.statusToday: Harmless. Each half stays internally consistent — sample.py keeps calling the pre-eviction `shipped_items`, which raises the pre-eviction class — and the 191-test suite is green.
knownHazards.whenItBites: The first `except SuiteInputMissing` that crosses the boundary (a stage catching what a re-imported validator raised) stops catching, silently, with no test failure.
knownHazards.fix: Move the exception into a module the registry never evicts. That module does not exist and `coursekit/__init__.py` is owned by the scaffold lane, so this is filed rather than done. A comment at the import in sample.py points here.

knownHazards.what: `coursekit sample es --n 300`, the spelling in this lane's brief, does not exist. Per-stage options ride on `--set` for all seven verbs.
knownHazards.statusToday: The capability is present under the sanctioned spelling: `--set n=300 --set seed=20260911`, and a bare `coursekit sample es` already draws REVIEWER_SAMPLE_ITEMS = 300, which is what the plan's P2 row asks for. tools/coursekit/README.md says this in as many words.
knownHazards.whenItBites: Never functionally; only if somebody types the brief's spelling.
knownHazards.fix: Two lines in `cli.py`, whose docstring deliberately forbids per-stage flags ('P2 runs as two waves over eight lanes; a hand-maintained dispatch table here would be eight conflicting edits to one function'). Not this lane's file and not this lane's call to overturn.

knownHazards.what: `build-es` and `validate-es` in pack-ci.yml have never executed. `pipeline-ready` counts 0/10 stages and 3/17 validators today (only V10-V12 exist), so both long jobs are skipped by their `if:` guard.
knownHazards.statusToday: The two jobs are actionlint-clean and nothing more. The capped ingest, the full G0-G9, the V1-V4 100% assertion, the 120 MB `du -sb` audio budget and the `es-pack-<sha>` artefact upload are all UNRUN.
knownHazards.whenItBites: The first phase where the G-lanes are all registered — the jobs go live and any mistake in them surfaces then.
knownHazards.fix: Nothing to fix here; it is a sequencing fact. The integrator should expect the first green `pipeline-ready` to be the first real run of both jobs.

knownHazards.what: docs/ci.md's workflow table still describes pack-ci as '`coursekit validate` on content changes' and does not mention `coursekit`, `pipeline-ready`, `build-es` or `validate-es`.
knownHazards.statusToday: Stale documentation. docs/ci.md is not in this lane's file list.
knownHazards.whenItBites: A reader trusts the table over the workflow.
knownHazards.fix: One table row, for whoever owns docs/ci.md.
